title: No circuit breaker for exhausted API credits mid-run in bootstrap pipeline
description: _check_openrouter_credits() (bootstrap/orchestrate.py:121) only checks once, before Stage 1. If credits run out mid-run, each subsequent module's LLMClient.generate call burns through _generate_openrouter's full 3-retry exponential backoff (llm_client.py:471-529) against a guaranteed-failing key, then the outer except Exception as exc: ... SYNTHESIS_SKIP (orchestrate.py:508, :1092) swallows the failure and moves to the next module -- repeating the same doomed retry cascade for every remaining module instead of aborting fast with a clear 'credits exhausted' signal. This is very likely what caused the stalled bootstrap run in project memory to stop at 11/100 without a clean error.
design: Related project memory: bootstrap pipeline stalled 11/100 modules in on 2026-05-25 due to exhausted OpenRouter credits -- this is the likely root cause of the silent stall.
acceptance_criteria: A credit/quota-exhaustion error from the LLM provider is detected and short-circuits the remaining run with a clear top-level error, instead of retrying and silently skipping every remaining module.

title: Bootstrap resume can silently adopt unverified partial output as 'passed'
description: bootstrap/orchestrate.py:431 (_synthesis_loop) and :947 (_synthesis_loop_ts) treat any .py/.ts file present in out_dir as proof of a passed, verified module and skip re-synthesis on rerun. But files are written by the TDD runner mid-iteration, BEFORE the clean-room/style gate loop (lines 482-506, 1028-1085) runs. If the process is killed (OOM, SIGKILL, exhausted API credits) after a file is written but before verification, a rerun adopts unverified -- possibly clean-room-failing or private-code-leaking -- output as done. The .spec.sha256 cache-bust check only detects a changed spec, not an incomplete prior run. Directly relevant to the currently-stalled bootstrap run (11/100 modules done, stopped on exhausted OpenRouter credits per project memory) -- resuming it as-is risks silently baking in unverified modules.
design: Related project memory: bootstrap pipeline stalled 11/100 modules in on 2026-05-25 due to exhausted OpenRouter credits.
acceptance_criteria: A '.verified' marker (or equivalent) is written only after the clean-room/style gate passes; resume logic checks for that marker, not just file presence, before skipping re-synthesis of a module.
notes: Found during 2026-08-05 security/risk/resilience audit (resilience review). Blocks safely resuming the stalled bootstrap run -- fix before re-running with topped-up credits.

title: TypeScriptWorkerAgent impl prompt never reads playbook rules
description:
The shared bootstrap playbook contains style rules in the strategies_and_hard_rules section (camelCase identifiers, no Math.random(), no bitwise hash, no Python idioms). These rules are never injected into the synthesis prompts.

Root cause:
- _get_test_rules() reads only the test_assertion_rules section and only injects into the test prompt
- _impl_prompt() builds its prompt with no playbook lookup at all
- strategies_and_hard_rules is populated but never consumed by the worker

The result: the model repeatedly generates snake_case identifiers, bitwise hash functions, and Math.random() defaults in implementation files — exactly the mistakes the rules are meant to prevent. The style gate catches them and deletes the output, but the model never learns because the rules don't reach it.

Fix: _impl_prompt() (and _refactor_prompt()) should load strategies_and_hard_rules bullets and inject them as a hard constraints block in the prompt, alongside the existing Gherkin context.
close_reason: Closed

title: Playbook seed bullets don't persist to disk between runs
description:
The bootstrap pipeline calls _seed_shared_playbook() at the start of each TypeScript synthesis run, which reports adding 15 bullets to the shared playbook. But bootstrap_ts_shared.json on disk always shows 0 bullets after a run completes.

Two likely causes:
1. _save_playbook() is failing silently (exception swallowed) after add_bullet() calls
2. PlaybookManager is writing to a different path than expected

Impact: Every run starts from scratch with no accumulated knowledge. The improvement loop never fires — the model keeps making the same mistakes (snake_case, Math.random(), bitwise hash) because the corrective rules don't survive between sessions.

To reproduce: run bootstrap/orchestrate.py --lang typescript, observe 'added 15 bullets' in output, then check data/playbooks/bootstrap_ts_shared.json — it will show 0 bullets in all sections.
close_reason: Closed

title: PodmanRunner: real ContainerRunner using rootless Podman
description:
## Why this exists

All current ContainerRunner implementations (SubprocessRunner, HashingSubprocessRunner, BanditSubprocessRunner) run pytest and bandit directly on the host. The Safety Sandwich provides verified correctness but zero process/filesystem isolation. PodmanRunner is the production implementation that gives real isolation guarantees.

## What to build

src/agents/podman_runner.py — PodmanRunner class implementing the ContainerRunner protocol:

- start(): pull image if needed, podman run -d --name {name} {image} sleep infinity, pip install pytest bandit inside container
- stop(): podman rm -f {name}
- is_alive(): podman inspect {name} — checks container is in running state
- send_pulse(code_path): podman cp → podman exec pytest → podman exec bandit → podman exec sha256 → return PulseResult with all fields populated

Container lifecycle: persistent sidecar (start once, exec per pulse). Name is unique per instance (harness_{uuid8}).
Default image: python:3.12-slim.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PodmanRunner satisfies ContainerRunner protocol (isinstance check passes)
- [ ] start() launches a named rootless container and installs pytest + bandit
- [ ] send_pulse() returns PulseResult with exit_code, stdout, stderr, bandit counts, h_executed, bandit_clean
- [ ] stop() removes the container cleanly
- [ ] is_alive() returns False before start() and after stop()
- [ ] Integration tests skip gracefully when podman is not in PATH
- [ ] PodmanOrchestrator.pulse() works end-to-end with a real PodmanRunner (integration test, skipif no podman)

title: Bandit gate: static analysis inside sidecar container
description:
## What to build

Add Bandit static analysis as a hard gate inside the sidecar container. After pytest runs, the container runs bandit -r on the code file and includes severity counts in the response. LV treats HIGH severity findings as a hard failure equivalent to a test failure.

Changes:
- Container entrypoint: after pytest, run bandit -r <file> --format json; parse output for HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW counts.
- Response payload: extend with bandit_high, bandit_medium, bandit_low counts and bandit_clean bool.
- LV side (PodmanOrchestrator.pulse): if bandit_high > 0, return a failed PhaseResult regardless of pytest exit_code; include Bandit output in the error field.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Bandit runs inside the container on every pulse (not on the host)
- [ ] Response payload includes severity counts
- [ ] bandit_high > 0 causes pulse() to return passed=False
- [ ] MEDIUM and LOW findings are logged but not blocking
- [ ] A file containing os.system() call fails the Bandit gate
- [ ] A clean file passes the Bandit gate without adding measurable latency beyond < 200ms

title: Hash-Lock protocol: SHA-256 reconciliation (H_proposed ≡ H_executed)
description:
## What to build

Add the Hash-Lock integrity layer to the sidecar communication protocol. Before writing code to tmpfs, LV generates H_proposed. The container hashes the file it actually ran and returns H_executed. LV asserts equality before accepting the result.

Changes:
- LV side (PodmanOrchestrator.pulse): compute hashlib.sha256 of the code string before writing to tmpfs; include H_proposed in the socket request payload.
- Container side (entrypoint): after receiving the file, hash it; include H_executed in the response payload.
- LV reconciliation: assert H_proposed == H_executed; raise SecurityBreachError with details if they diverge.
- SecurityBreachError is a new exception class that logs the mismatch and nukes the tmpfs file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] H_proposed computed on the code string (not the file) before tmpfs write
- [ ] H_executed computed on the file bytes inside the container
- [ ] LV raises SecurityBreachError when hashes diverge
- [ ] SecurityBreachError includes both hashes in the error message for auditability
- [ ] Hashing adds < 5ms overhead for standard Python modules (tested)
- [ ] Unit test: tampered file (simulate divergence) triggers SecurityBreachError

## Blocked by

- ace_enterprise-2j2 (Sidecar Foundation)
close_reason: Closed

title: LibCST import whitelist filter (LV-side pre-filter)
description:
## What to build

Implement the top layer of the Safety Sandwich: an LV-side ImportFilter that rejects code strings containing forbidden imports before they ever reach the container. This is pure host-side logic with no container dependency.

Components:
- ImportFilter class (src/agents/import_filter.py): uses stdlib ast to parse the code string and walk import nodes; raises ForbiddenImportError if any import matches the blocklist.
- Default blocklist: os, subprocess, socket, sys, shutil, ctypes.
- Blocked builtins (call detection): eval, exec.
- Blocklist is configurable (passed at construction).

Note: LibCST is deferred to the automated refactoring layer — ast is sufficient here since we are analyzing, not rewriting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] ForbiddenImportError is raised for import os, from subprocess import run, etc.
- [x] Clean code (no forbidden imports) passes through without error
- [x] Blocklist is configurable, not hardcoded
- [x] Unit tests cover: direct import, from-import, aliased import, nested import, and a clean file
- [x] No new dependencies required (stdlib ast)

title: Sidecar Foundation: PodmanOrchestrator + Unix socket channel
description:
## What to build

Build the foundational infrastructure for the Clean Room isolation layer. This is a thin end-to-end slice that proves the Podman sidecar can receive a Python file via Unix domain socket, run pytest, and return results — with no integration into python_language_pod.py yet.

- Smoke test: write a trivial passing test to the tmpfs, pulse the orchestrator, assert pytest output comes back clean.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Container starts rootless with --network none and --cap-drop=all
- [ ] Host-side tmpfs is mounted so code never touches persistent disk
- [ ] Unix socket listener in container receives a file path and returns pytest output
- [ ] PodmanOrchestrator.pulse(code_path) returns exit_code + stdout/stderr

title: Parse error in _get_next_increment triggers false 'requirement satisfied' early exit
description: When the LLM returns a malformed increment (wrong pipe-count or unparseable), _get_next_increment returns None. The caller treats None as COMPLETE and exits the TDD loop after 1 cycle. Found during garden-twin construction feature run where cycle 2 returned '_calculate_picket__positions |' (3 parts instead of 4).

title: RedundancyPreChecker falsely blocks distinct-entity tests with same operation verb

title: TDD agent misinterprets feature requirements and ignores project-aware placement
description:
**Bug:** TDD agent creates wrong class/file types and places files in wrong directories despite project-aware TDD integration.

**Observed Behavior:**
1. Feature file specifies "DynamicModelRouter class in src/broker/dynamic_model_router.py"
2. TDD agent creates "CostQualityAnalyzer" class in "src/cost_quality.py" instead
3. Project-aware placement code is integrated but not effective

**Root Cause Analysis:**
1. **Feature misinterpretation:** LLM reads feature scenarios about "cost" and "quality" and generates analyzer code instead of router code, ignoring explicit class name requirements
2. **Placement keyword mismatch:** `_determine_impl_path()` uses per-test `description` text for keyword matching (e.g., "calculate cost efficiency metrics"), not the original feature requirement which contains "routing" and "broker"
3. **No explicit class/file constraints:** The LLM prompt doesn't enforce the class name or file path specified in the feature file

**Expected Behavior:**
1. Feature file Background states: "a new DynamicModelRouter class to be created in src/broker/dynamic_model_router.py"
2. TDD agent should create `DynamicModelRouter` class
3. File should be placed in `src/broker/` per project structure

**Fix Required:**
1. **Pass original feature requirement to placement logic:** Store the feature requirement at build start and use it for all file placement decisions, not per-test descriptions
2. **Extract explicit paths from Gherkin:** Parse Background section for explicit file paths and class names, use these as constraints
3. **Add class/file constraints to LLM prompt:** Include explicit instructions like "You MUST create class named DynamicModelRouter" and "File MUST be placed in src/broker/"
4. **Validate generated filenames:** Check if generated filename matches feature requirement before writing

**Files to modify:**
- src/agents/autonomous_tdd_agent.py - Store feature requirement, pass to placement
- src/agents/project_aware_tdd.py - Add method to extract explicit paths from Gherkin
- _plan_increments() and _determine_next_increment() - Use feature-level placement

**Reproduction:**
```bash
python -c "
from mcp_server.tools import ACETools
tools = ACETools(enable_tdd=True)
result = tools.call_tool('build_feature', {
    'feature': 'Dynamic model routing with DynamicModelRouter class',
    'project_path': '/home/ch_dev/ace_enterprise',
    'gherkin_dir': 'features',
    'model': 'google/gemini-2.0-flash-001'
})
"
# Result: Creates src/cost_quality.py with CostQualityAnalyzer instead of src/broker/dynamic_model_router.py with DynamicModelRouter
```

title: Project-aware TDD agent with code reuse detection
description:
**Problem:** TDD agent dumps all files into flat test_dir/src_dir without understanding project structure. Results in:
- Files in wrong locations (e.g., broker code in src/ root instead of src/broker/)
- Reinventing existing utilities instead of importing them
- Not following project conventions

**Solution:** Add project structure awareness before code generation:

**Phase 1: Structure Discovery**
1. Use codebase-memory-mcp `get_architecture()` to understand project layout
2. Build map of: folder purposes, module responsibilities, naming conventions
3. Cache structure for session (don't re-analyze every cycle)

**Phase 2: Smart File Placement**
1. Before creating TestIncrement, determine correct subdirectory based on:
   - Feature type (broker, agent, storage, utils, etc.)
   - Related existing code location
   - Project conventions
2. Update TestIncrement.test_file and implementation_file paths accordingly

**Phase 3: Code Reuse Detection**
1. Before generating implementation, use `search_graph()` to find:
   - Existing similar functions/classes
   - Utilities that could be imported
   - Base classes to extend
2. Include reuse suggestions in LLM prompt for GREEN phase
3. Prefer imports over reimplementation

**Phase 4: Convention Matching**
1. Analyze existing code for patterns:
   - Naming conventions (snake_case, class naming)
   - Import style (absolute vs relative)
   - Docstring format
   - Type hint usage
2. Instruct LLM to follow discovered conventions

**Files to modify:**
- src/agents/autonomous_tdd_agent.py - Add structure awareness
- src/agents/project_analyzer.py (new) - Project structure analysis

**Integration with codebase-memory-mcp:**
- get_architecture() - folder structure, package layout
- search_graph() - find reusable code
- search_code() - find pattern examples

**Acceptance criteria:**
- New broker code goes to src/broker/, not src/
- Agent suggests importing existing utilities instead of rewriting
- Generated code follows project naming conventions
- File placement matches existing project structure

title: Add semantic code quality evaluation (AST analysis)
description:
**Gap:** Current evaluation focuses on syntax validity and test passing. No semantic analysis of code design quality, maintainability, or security.

**Problem:**
- BlindEvaluator scores: syntax (30pts) + structure (20pts) + tests (50pts)
- A syntactically correct but poorly-designed solution scores same as good design
- No detection of: high cyclomatic complexity, code smells, security issues, SOLID violations

**Solution:**
1. Create SemanticCodeAnalyzer class with AST-based analysis
2. Add quality dimensions:
   - Cyclomatic complexity score

4. Weight: syntax (20) + structure (15) + tests (40) + semantic (25)

**New scoring rubric:**
- Complexity penalty: -5 pts per function with complexity > 10
- Security penalty: -10 pts per critical issue (eval, hardcoded secrets)

title: Module-level contracts for stateful systems
description:
Current limitation: Contract-driven TDD tests each function in isolation, but stateful systems (like inventory management) have interdependent functions that share state.

Problem:
- get_total_value() needs add_item() to be called first
- Tests can't pass without proper state setup
- Fixtures help but don't fully solve the problem

Solution needed:
- Generate module-level contracts (all functions together)
- Build the module as a unit
- Test end-to-end rather than per-function

This would change the flow from:
  contract per function → implement each → test each

To:
  module contract → implement all functions together → integration tests

title: Harden podman container flags: --read-only, --cap-drop=all, --security-opt=no-new-privileges
description: src/agents/podman_runner.py:64-86 podman run command sets --network none, cpu/memory limits, and --init, but no --read-only, no --cap-drop=all, and no --security-opt=no-new-privileges. Container currently has the full default Linux capability set (including CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE). This means generated code running in the sandbox has filesystem write access to its own workspace and could in principle self-modify its own test/impl files during execution (the canonical_hash pulse check in podman_orchestrator.py exists specifically to detect this after the fact -- see conversation 2026-08-05/09 audit). Making the workspace mount read-only during execution would close this class of tampering structurally rather than just detecting it, but --read-only alone is insufficient: a process retaining CAP_SYS_ADMIN can remount a read-only mount as read-write, so cap-drop and no-new-privileges must ship together with it. Implementation note: the workspace is currently chmod 0o777 (podman_runner.py:60-62) because some tooling (e.g. vitest .timestamp cache files) needs to write into it -- a blanket read-only workspace would break that, so cache writes may need to be relocated to the already-writable tmpfs /tmp mount instead of the bind-mounted workspace.
design: Files touched: src/agents/podman_runner.py, src/agents/typescript_runner.py. No changes to Containerfile/Containerfile.ts needed (rootless podman + user namespace remap already require the world-readable chmod 0o777 for the container's mapped uid to read workspace files, and that still holds since the write bit stopped being load-bearing once the mount itself enforces read-only).
acceptance_criteria: podman run adds --cap-drop=all and --security-opt=no-new-privileges for both PodmanRunner (Python) and TypeScriptRunner. Workspace bind mount is read-only during test/impl execution while still allowing the host-side process to clear/rewrite it between pulses; any tool cache writes (e.g. vitest .timestamp) are relocated to the tmpfs /tmp mount instead of the workspace. canonical_hash pulse check (podman_orchestrator.py) is retained as defense-in-depth after these flags are added, not removed.
notes:
Implemented and verified 2026-08-09. src/agents/podman_runner.py: added --cap-drop=all + --security-opt=no-new-privileges, and mounted the workspace :ro (both PodmanRunner and TypeScriptRunner, which inherits start()). Python side needed python -B and pytest -p no:cacheprovider to avoid writing bytecode/cache to the now-read-only workspace. TypeScript side needed more surgery than the original description anticipated: TypeScriptRunner previously created a node_modules symlink and wrote vitest.config.ts directly into the workspace via podman exec/host write -- both broke under :ro because (a) the symlink creation is a container-side write, moved to a host-side Path.symlink_to() instead since the host retains full write access to the underlying directory outside the container's mount view, and (b) Vite's config loader bundles vitest.config.ts and writes a compiled .timestamp-*.mjs file NEXT TO the config file regardless of cacheDir -- moved the config itself off the workspace entirely, into the container's writable /tmp via podman cp, with its own /tmp/node_modules symlink (created once in an overridden start()) so 'vitest/config' still resolves from the new location.

Verified: all 12 existing tests/test_podman_runner.py integration tests pass unchanged against real podman. Manually verified TypeScriptRunner end-to-end (pass case, fail case, 3x repeated pulses on the same hot container) since no automated TS integration suite exists. Proved the actual security property with a live tamper test: generated Python code that tries to rewrite its own test file mid-run now gets 'Read-only file system' (Errno 30) instead of silently faking a pass -- confirms the read-only mount, not just the pre-existing canonical_hash check, now blocks self-modification at the OS level.
close_reason: Implemented, tested against real podman (12/12 existing tests pass, manual TS end-to-end verification, live tamper test confirms self-modification is now OS-level blocked). See notes for implementation details and the TS-side complications encountered.

title: No prompt-injection / content validation on playbook bullet writes (playbook poisoning)

title: Import blocklist bypassable via importlib/__import__/globals()

title: PolyglotTDDRunner: orchestrate multi-language pod loop and report token efficiency
description:
## What to build

A thin orchestrator that wires the existing LanguagePod implementations into a runnable end-to-end loop. Nothing in src/ currently calls run_red/run_green/run_refactor outside the pod files themselves, so the multi-language support has no entry point.

Implement PolyglotTDDRunner in src/agents/polyglot_tdd_runner.py:

- PolyglotTDDRunner(pod_factory, reporter=TokenEfficiencyReporter) constructor
- run(feature_requirement, test_file, implementation_file, languages, max_cycles=5) method that:
  1. Creates the appropriate pod for each requested language via pod_factory
  2. Drives RED → GREEN → REFACTOR per pod, retrying GREEN up to max_cycles times
  3. Collects PodRun data (language, feature_requirement, token_usage, cycles_to_green)
  4. Returns PolyglotRunResult containing per-language PhaseResults and an EfficiencyReport

- PodFactory with create(language, ...) that returns PythonLanguagePod or GoLanguagePod
- PolyglotRunResult dataclass: language_results dict, efficiency_report EfficiencyReport

The runner does not need to replace AutonomousTDDAgent — it is additive, operating through the LanguagePod protocol.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PolyglotTDDRunner.run() drives RED→GREEN→REFACTOR for each requested language
- [ ] GREEN is retried up to max_cycles if it fails; cycles_to_green reflects actual attempts
- [ ] PolyglotRunResult.efficiency_report is an EfficiencyReport from TokenEfficiencyReporter
- [ ] PodFactory.create("python", agent) returns a PythonLanguagePod
- [ ] PodFactory.create("go", llm_client) returns a GoLanguagePod
- [ ] Unsupported language raises ValueError with the language name

title: Audit hash-chain is not tamper-evident against a privileged DB attacker
description: src/audit/store.py:276-320 verify_chain() checks each event's prev_hash against the prior row's event_hash entirely within the same Postgres table. A DB admin, or anyone with write access to the audit table (compromised credential, insider), can rewrite the entire table end-to-end with a freshly-computed, internally-consistent chain and verify_chain() will still pass -- there's no external anchoring (no periodic hash publication, no WORM storage, no signing key held outside the DB). For a system whose stated purpose is a tamper-evident model-attribution audit trail, this undermines the core guarantee against the most realistic threat.
acceptance_criteria: Chain integrity is anchored outside the mutable DB -- e.g. periodic hash checkpoints published to an external append-only store (git, S3 Object Lock, a separate signing service), or events are signed with a key not accessible to the DB role that can write the events table.
notes: Re-triaged 2026-08-05: downgraded from P1. Threat model (privileged/compromised DB credential belonging to someone other than the operator) doesn't apply while single-user -- the only person with DB access is the same person the audit trail is meant to hold accountable. Re-raise once there are multiple operators or the audit trail needs to be trusted against its own admins.

title: Bandit gate runs after code execution, not before -- rename/document to avoid false confidence
description: src/agents/podman_runner.py:119-137 send_pulse() executes pytest first, then runs Bandit afterward. title: Harden ImportFilter against dynamic import patterns
description:
## Why this exists

The ImportFilter (ace_enterprise-sfy) walks AST import nodes and catches `import os`, `from os import ...`, etc. The Bandit gate (ace_enterprise-c5d) catches shell injection via variable arguments (HIGH severity). However, neither layer blocks dynamic import patterns that bypass static AST analysis:

- `__import__('os').system('...')`
- `importlib.import_module('os').system('...')`
- `getattr(__builtins__, '__import__')('os')`

Bandit rates these LOW (hardcoded string argument) or does not flag them at all. The ImportFilter does not walk `Call` nodes for `__import__` or `importlib`.

This gap only matters if the LLM is actively adversarial rather than naively writing dangerous code — standard bad code is caught at layer 1. But it is a known hole in the Safety Sandwich.

## What needs to be done

Extend ImportFilter.check() to walk ast.Call nodes and detect:
- calls to `__import__` where the first argument is a string matching the blocklist
- calls to `importlib.import_module` where the argument matches the blocklist

Add unit tests for each dynamic pattern alongside existing import tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `__import__('os')` raises ForbiddenImportError
- [ ] `importlib.import_module('subprocess')` raises ForbiddenImportError
- [ ] Non-blocked dynamic imports (e.g. `__import__('json')`) pass through
- [ ] Existing ImportFilter tests continue to pass
notes:
Implemented and verified 2026-08-09. src/agents/import_filter.py: added _collect_dynamic_import_aliases() (tracks importlib module aliases and importlib.import_module aliases, including renamed imports) and _check_dynamic_import_call() (catches __import__(...) and importlib.import_module(...) calls, checking the first arg when it's a string literal against the existing blocklist). All 4 acceptance criteria met: __import__('os') raises, importlib.import_module('subprocess') raises, __import__('json') passes through, existing tests unchanged (all pass). Added 8 new tests to tests/test_import_filter.py covering the acceptance criteria plus alias renaming and non-literal-arg (can't-statically-prove) cases.

Explicitly NOT covered (documented as advisory-layer limitation, verified live): globals()['__builtins__'].__import__('os') — attribute-indirection via dict subscript is not realistically catchable by static AST pattern matching without a much more invasive analysis, and this is consistent with the filter's role as a narrowing layer, not the security boundary. That specific bypass is still contained by the read-only workspace mount + --network none + --cap-drop=all from ace_enterprise-bwe regardless of whether this filter catches it.

Found and left alone (out of scope, pre-existing, confirmed via git stash before/after comparison): tests/test_python_language_pod.py and tests/test_hazardous_m2_forbidden_import.py have 23 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (PythonLanguagePod.__init__ signature drift vs test fixtures — tests pass project_root/orchestrator as missing args). Worth its own ticket if not already tracked.
close_reason: Implemented: importlib.import_module(...) and __import__(...) with string-literal args are now caught. 18/18 tests pass (10 original + 8 new). Verified live against the exact attack strings from the original audit.

title: Add quality prediction with Bayesian confidence intervals
description:
**Gap:** Metrics provide success rate but no predictive confidence intervals. Cannot quantify uncertainty about future performance.

**Problem:**
- 100% success on 5 tasks != 100% confidence on next 1000 tasks
- No way to express "we need more data" vs "high confidence"
- reliability_score uses hardcoded thresholds (<5, <20 tasks)

**Solution:**
1. Implement Bayesian estimation for success rates
   - Beta-binomial model for success/failure
   - Credible intervals (e.g., 95% CI)
   - Prior based on model family averages
2. Replace hardcoded reliability thresholds with statistical certainty
3. Report confidence intervals in performance queries
4. Flag "insufficient data" when CI width exceeds threshold

**Statistical model:**
```
Prior: Beta(alpha=1, beta=1)  # uniform
Posterior: Beta(alpha + successes, beta + failures)
CI = beta.interval(0.95, alpha_post, beta_post)
```

**Files to modify:**
- src/broker/performance_aggregator.py - Add Bayesian estimation
- src/broker/adaptive_broker.py - Use CI in routing decisions

**Dependencies:** scipy or numpy for beta distribution

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Success rates reported with 95% CI
- Routing considers uncertainty (prefers known-good over uncertain)
- "Insufficient data" flag when CI > 0.3 width
close_reason: Bayesian Beta-Binomial model implemented in src/broker/bayesian.py; wired into AgentPerformanceMetrics.bayesian_estimate; AdaptiveBroker._calculate_score uses ci_lower as conservative base score; 19 tests in tests/test_bayesian_routing.py all passing
